data.name: Weather.Subtitle
data.value: Each customer gets a weather report drawn from their payment history. Lettra uses it to predict when each open invoice should be paid.

data.name: Weather.Forecast.Hint
data.value: Each open invoice is expected on its due date, shifted by its customer's usual delay, never before tomorrow. Cash planning can reuse these amounts.

data.name: Weather.Empty.Text
data.value: The weather appears once validated invoices have been paid or have reached their due date.

data.name: Weather.Why.Overdue
data.value: An invoice has been waiting for payment {0} days past its due date.

data.name: Weather.Why.Unknown
data.value: Fewer than two invoices paid or due: Lettra needs more history.

data.name: Weather.Rules
data.value: How Lettra works out the weather

data.name: Weather.Rule.Sunny
data.value: pays at most 2 days after the due date on average, the time a transfer takes.

data.name: Weather.Rule.Cloudy
data.value: pays 3 to 10 days after the due date on average.

data.name: Weather.Rule.Rainy
data.value: pays 11 to 30 days after the due date on average.

data.name: Weather.Rule.Stormy
data.value: pays more than a month after the due date on average, or one of their invoices is more than 60 days overdue.

data.name: Weather.Rule.Unknown
data.value: fewer than two invoices paid or due over the last twelve months.

data.name: Weather.Rules.Hint
data.value: The average delay is weighted by amounts; an overdue invoice still unpaid counts with its delay so far. The best day to send compares payment delays by the day the invoice was issued. These are simple statistics, worked out each time the screen opens: no AI, nothing is written to the dossier.

data.name: Weather.Doubtful
data.value: Doubtful: {0} of invoices more than {1} days overdue, left out of the forecast. Better chase them.

data.name: Audit.Subtitle
data.value: Lettra runs on the FEC the tests a tax inspector would run with their tools, and tells you what they would point out before they do.

data.name: Audit.Other.Title
data.value: Check a FEC from another software

data.name: Audit.Other.Hint
data.value: Pick a FEC (tab or pipe separated text): the same tests run, over the period above.

data.name: Audit.Result.Title
data.value: What the inspector would point out in {0}

data.name: Audit.Verdict.Clean
data.value: None of the {0} tests finds anything.

data.name: Audit.Verdict.Findings
data.value: {0} point(s) the inspector would raise, {1} question(s) they would ask.

data.name: Audit.Verdict.Unreadable
data.value: This file is not a readable FEC (header or columns): no test could run.

data.name: Audit.Benford.Hint
data.value: In real amounts the first digit is a 1 about three times in ten and a 9 less than once in twenty. Blue bar: your amounts; grey bar: the law.

data.name: Audit.Disclaimer
data.value: This is practice, not tax advice: nothing is sent to the tax office, and an inspector has other sources (bank statements, cross-checks). The tests and their thresholds are described in the documentation.

data.name: Audit.Check.Format.Why
data.value: Does the file follow article A47 A-1: columns, dates, amounts, balanced entries? A non-compliant FEC can be fined.

data.name: Audit.Check.Format.Fix
data.value: Fix it in the software that produces the FEC and export it again; the FEC tab shows the details line by line.

data.name: Audit.Check.EntryNumberGap.Why
data.value: In each journal, entries follow each other with no gap: a missing number suggests a deleted entry.

data.name: Audit.Check.EntryNumberGap.Fix
data.value: Find the reason for each gap (cancelled entry, change of year) and keep a written record.

data.name: Audit.Check.PieceNumberGap.Why
data.value: Invoices are numbered in one continuous sequence: a missing number suggests an undeclared sale.

data.name: Audit.Check.PieceNumberGap.Found
data.value: {0} document number(s) missing from the sales journal.

data.name: Audit.Check.PieceNumberGap.Fix
data.value: Check whether the document exists outside the period (before or after); otherwise prepare its explanation.

data.name: Audit.Check.SundayOrHoliday
data.value: Entries on a Sunday or public holiday

data.name: Audit.Check.SundayOrHoliday.Why
data.value: Activity on a closed day is possible (retail, late entry), but the inspector asks why.

data.name: Audit.Check.SundayOrHoliday.Found
data.value: {0} entry(ies) dated on a Sunday or public holiday.

data.name: Audit.Check.SundayOrHoliday.Passed
data.value: No entry on a closed day.

data.name: Audit.Check.SundayOrHoliday.Fix
data.value: If the business opens on those days, nothing to do; otherwise check the document date.

data.name: Audit.Check.LateValidation
data.value: Entries validated long after their date

data.name: Audit.Check.LateValidation.Why
data.value: More than 60 days between an entry's date and its validation: the inspector looks for backdated entries.

data.name: Audit.Check.LateValidation.Found
data.value: {0} entry(ies) validated more than 60 days after their date.

data.name: Audit.Check.LateValidation.Passed
data.value: Every entry is validated in time.

data.name: Audit.Check.LateValidation.Fix
data.value: Keep the document that explains the delay (invoice received late, year-end adjustment).

data.name: Audit.Check.NegativeCash.Why
data.value: A till cannot pay out more than it holds: a negative balance suggests unrecorded takings.

data.name: Audit.Check.NegativeCash.Found
data.value: {0} day(s) where cash ends negative (down to {1}).

data.name: Audit.Check.NegativeCash.Fix
data.value: Find the missing cash takings or fix the dates of cash outflows.

data.name: Audit.Check.CashOverLimit.Why
data.value: A cash payment exceeds the €1,000 legal ceiling (French monetary and financial code, article L112-6).

data.name: Audit.Check.CashOverLimit.Passed
data.value: No cash movement above the ceiling.

data.name: Audit.Check.CashOverLimit.Fix
data.value: Check it is a bank deposit or withdrawal, not a payment between businesses.

data.name: Audit.Check.RoundAmounts.Why
data.value: Entries of €1,000 or more landing exactly on the hundred are rare in real business and common in estimates.

data.name: Audit.Check.RoundAmounts.Found
data.value: {0} round entry(ies), {1}% of entries of €1,000 or more.

data.name: Audit.Check.RoundAmounts.Passed
data.value: Few round amounts ({1}% of entries of €1,000 or more).

data.name: Audit.Check.RoundAmounts.Fix
data.value: Keep the document behind each round amount (contract, flat fee, down payment).

data.name: Audit.Check.DuplicateLines.Why
data.value: Same day, same account, same amount and same label in two entries: a double entry inflates costs or sales.

data.name: Audit.Check.DuplicateLines.Fix
data.value: If these are two real operations, make their labels distinct; otherwise reverse the duplicate.

data.name: Audit.Check.Benford.Why
data.value: The first digit of real amounts follows a known law; made-up amounts drift away from it.

data.name: Audit.Check.Benford.Found
data.value: Mean deviation of {1} point(s) over {0} amounts: the series drifts from the law.

data.name: Audit.Check.Benford.Passed
data.value: {0} amounts read; mean deviation of {1} point(s), within the norm.

data.name: Audit.Check.Benford.TooFew
data.value: Only {0} amount(s) of at least €10: the test needs 200 to be conclusive.

data.name: Audit.Check.Benford.Fix
data.value: Look at the digits furthest away: they often reveal a repeated flat fee or a series typed by hand.

data.name: Audit.Check.CustomerCredit.Why
data.value: A customer who overpaid, or a forgotten invoice: the inspector asks what the balance stands for.

data.name: Audit.Check.CustomerCredit.Fix
data.value: Match the payment with its invoice, or refund the overpayment.

data.name: Audit.Check.SupplierDebit.Why
data.value: A supplier paid with no recorded invoice: missing cost or down payment to justify.

data.name: Audit.Check.SupplierDebit.Fix
data.value: Record the missing purchase invoice or classify the down payment.

data.name: Audit.Check.VatRate.Why
data.value: Collected VAT over revenue cannot exceed the 20% standard rate.

data.name: Audit.Check.VatRate.Found
data.value: Collected VAT is {1}% of revenue: more than the standard rate.

data.name: Audit.Check.VatRate.Passed
data.value: Apparent collected VAT rate: {1}% of revenue.

data.name: Audit.Check.VatRate.Fix
data.value: Look for VAT counted twice or a sale recorded outside accounts 70.

data.name: Proof.Subtitle
data.value: Every validated invoice carries a QR code signed by the dossier. Paste the text read by a QR code reader here: Lettra tells you whether the invoice really comes from this dossier and has not been changed.

data.name: Proof.Code.Hint
data.value: The text starts with LETTRA-PREUVE-1. A phone camera reads the QR code and lets you copy this text.

data.name: Proof.Verdict.Authentic
data.value: Genuine invoice: signed by this dossier, and identical to the recorded document.

data.name: Proof.Verdict.Mismatch
data.value: Signed by this dossier, but the recorded document no longer says the same thing.

data.name: Proof.Verdict.Forged
data.value: Invalid signature: the text was changed after signing. Do not pay without checking.

data.name: Proof.Verdict.Foreign
data.value: This invoice was not issued by this dossier (its key is not in the registry).

data.name: Proof.Verdict.Unreadable
data.value: This text is not a Lettra proof.

data.name: Proof.Credited
data.value: This invoice is fully cancelled by one or more credit notes.

data.name: Proof.Difference.Missing
data.value: No validated document with this number in the dossier.

data.name: Proof.Difference.IssueDate
data.value: The issue date is not the same.

data.name: Proof.Difference.TotalInclTax
data.value: The total incl. VAT is not the same.

data.name: Proof.Difference.Siren
data.value: The company SIREN is not the same.

data.name: Proof.Offline.Hint
data.value: The signed text is the QR code without its last field; the last field is the ECDSA P-256 signature (SHA-256, DER format) in URL-safe base 64. With the dossier's public key below, OpenSSL checks it:

data.name: Proof.Keys.Empty
data.value: The dossier has no key yet: it is created with the first validated document.

data.name: AsOf.Subtitle
data.value: The file as it was at the moment you choose, replayed from the tamper-proof journal: revenue, VAT, invoices due and customer balances. Nothing is changed.

data.name: AsOf.Go
data.value: Show the file at that moment

data.name: AsOf.Empty
data.value: The file was still empty at that moment.

data.name: AsOf.Empty.Before
data.value: The file was still empty at that moment: its first document dates from {0}.

data.name: AsOf.Chain.Intact
data.value: Chain verified up to that moment: {0} entries replayed, none was altered.

data.name: AsOf.Chain.Broken
data.value: Warning: the chain shows an anomaly before that moment ({0} entries replayed). The alert centre tells you more.

data.name: AsOf.Since
data.value: Since then, {0} events have been written to the journal.

data.name: AsOf.Months.Hint
data.value: Excluding VAT, net of credit notes, by issue date, like the period closings.

data.name: AsOf.Documents.Empty
data.value: No invoice was due at that moment.

data.name: AsOf.Documents.Search
data.value: Search a number or a customer

data.name: AsOf.Customers.Empty
data.value: No customer had a balance at that moment.

data.name: AsOf.Closing
data.value: Last signed closing: {0}, period ending {1}, cumulative {2}.

data.name: AsOf.Rule.Journal
data.value: The tamper-proof journal keeps every validation, credit note, payment and closing, chained to the previous one. Lettra replays it up to the chosen moment and checks the chain on the way.

data.name: AsOf.Rule.Revenue
data.value: Revenue is that of the moment's year: invoices and down payments minus credit notes, by issue date.

data.name: AsOf.Rule.Due
data.value: An invoice's amount due is its total, minus the credit notes and payments recorded at that moment. A payment reversed later still counts.

data.name: AsOf.Rule.Today
data.value: The “today” amounts come from the current file, to show what has changed since. Customer names are today's.

data.name: Why.Subtitle
data.value: A figure from the home page broken down to the documents behind it, with the rule that produces it. Nothing is changed.

data.name: Why.Value.Overdue
data.value: including tax still due on invoices past their due date

data.name: Why.Term.Total
data.value: Total of overdue invoices incl. tax

data.name: Why.Rule.Text.MonthRevenue
data.value: It is the sum excluding tax of the {0} invoices and down payments issued from {1} to {2}, minus the {3} credit notes issued over the same period.

data.name: Why.Rule.Text.MonthRevenue.NoCredit
data.value: It is the sum excluding tax of the {0} invoices and down payments issued from {1} to {2}. No credit note was issued over the same period.

data.name: Why.Rule.Text.Future
data.value: {0} has not started yet: no document counts yet.

data.name: Why.Rule.Text.Overdue
data.value: It is what is still due on the {0} invoices past their due date on {1}: for each one, the total including tax, minus credit notes, minus what has been received.

data.name: Why.Same
data.value: The calculation is the home page's, with the same rules:

data.name: Why.Empty.MonthRevenue
data.value: No invoice or credit note issued this month.

data.name: Why.Empty.Overdue
data.value: No overdue invoice: nothing is due past its due date.

data.name: Why.Search
data.value: Search a document or a customer

data.name: Why.Rule.Deterministic
data.value: Lettra computes it without artificial intelligence: the same documents always give the same figure, and each document in the list opens in one click.

data.name: Why.Rule.MonthRevenue
data.value: A month's revenue counts invoices and down payments on their issue date, excluding tax, up to today for the current month. Credit notes issued in the month are subtracted. Drafts do not count.

data.name: Why.Rule.Overdue
data.value: An invoice is overdue when its due date has passed and something is left to pay. Down payments and credit notes have no due date to chase.

data.name: Why.Rule.Collected
data.value: What an invoice has received is the larger of what is recorded in Lettra and what is reported as collected to the platform: a payment never counts twice.

data.name: WhatIf.Subtitle
data.value: Try before you decide: grant more time, invoice before or after month end, change VAT scheme, hire. Lettra shows the effect on cash, VAT and deadlines.

data.name: WhatIf.Sandbox
data.value: Sandbox: nothing you try here is written to the file.

data.name: WhatIf.Delay.Hint
data.value: Every expected payment arrives that much later.

data.name: WhatIf.Vat.Hint
data.value: It applies to the trial invoice: return period, due date, or no VAT under the small business exemption.

data.name: WhatIf.Result
data.value: The effect over the next {0} weeks

data.name: WhatIf.Summary.None
data.value: No lever chosen: here is the expected cash as it stands.

data.name: WhatIf.Summary.More
data.value: With this scenario, cash is {0} higher after {1} weeks.

data.name: WhatIf.Summary.Less
data.value: With this scenario, cash is {0} lower after {1} weeks.

data.name: WhatIf.Invoice.Revenue
data.value: The invoice counts in the revenue of {0}, in the financial year ending on {1}.

data.name: WhatIf.Invoice.Vat
data.value: Its VAT of {0} is declared for {1} and paid on {2}.

data.name: WhatIf.Invoice.NoVat
data.value: Under the small business exemption, it carries no VAT.

data.name: WhatIf.Hire.Cost
data.value: The hire costs {0} a month with contributions, {1} over the {2} weeks and {3} over a year.

data.name: WhatIf.Effects.Empty
data.value: Nothing changes: pick a lever, then “Simulate”.

data.name: WhatIf.Rule.Baseline
data.value: The baseline is the payment weather forecast: each invoice due, expected on its due date shifted by the customer's usual delay. Doubtful invoices (more than 60 days late) are left out.

data.name: WhatIf.Rule.Delay
data.value: Extra time shifts every expected payment, and the trial invoice's due date, by that many days.

data.name: WhatIf.Rule.Invoice
data.value: The trial invoice counts in the revenue of its issue month and in the financial year containing that date.

data.name: WhatIf.Rule.Vat
data.value: Its VAT is declared for the period of its issue date (VAT on invoicing) and paid on the due date of the file's tax calendar. VAT on receipts and the annual CA12 are not simulated.

data.name: WhatIf.Rule.Hire
data.value: The hire costs gross salary plus employer contributions, paid on the last day of the month, pro rata for the first month. Adjust the contribution rate with the firm.

data.name: WhatIf.Rule.Sandbox
data.value: Lettra computes it without artificial intelligence, at each simulation. Nothing is written to the file.
